chatMessages.text: Here are 3 high-yield exam MCQs aligned with today’s lecture:
chatMessages.formula:
Q1. If d_k = 64, what is the attention scaling divisor?
    A) 64   B) 8 ✓   C) 32   D) 16

Q2. For symmetric matrix A = Aᵀ, eigenvectors of distinct λ are:
    A) Parallel   B) Orthogonal ✓   C) Zero   D) Singular

Q3. Which component prevents future tokens leaking in a decoder?
    A) LayerNorm   B) Causal Upper-Triangular Mask ✓   C) Dropout
chatMessages.formulaSub: Answer key marked with ✓ — ask me to explain any question!
chatMessages.detailBody: Watch for variance proofs on Q1: if qᵢ, kᵢ ~ N(0,1), then Var(q·k) = dₖ, so dividing by √dₖ brings Var((q·k)/√dₖ) back to 1.

chatMessages.text: Great question on "non verbal means". Here is the structured breakdown linked to your ENGLISH syllabus:
chatMessages.formula: Core Principle → Formalize Inputs → Apply ENGLISH Model → Verify Bounds
chatMessages.formulaSub: Tip: Enter any equation (e.g. x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0) or add a Gemini API key in Profile for open-ended live LLM queries.
chatMessages.detailBody: Break the problem into (1) assumptions and state dimensions, (2) governing equation or algorithm invariant, and (3) edge-case verification. You can also click "Quiz Me" or open Scan & Solve to capture handwritten work.
